details:
cutekitten-test@1.0.1 describes itself as a security test package for a school project and has no functional code. Its preinstall script runs `node preinstall.js` on npm install, which POSTs the machine's hostname, the OS username and the local time to the Discord webhook `https://canary.discord.com/api/webhooks/1566232728179843243/pM5rDIrCRrEpQRbA7ibaiQk1XOQlIftmBacA5s8jD8NvXn5W-rS832DOWHQS-G-j3N6U` as "PC Notifier". It was published by the npm account cutekitten05, which used the same script in wallet-adapter-base, axelarjs-sdk, bigbob22-test and sol-wallet-adapter on 2026-11-01.

## Source: amazon-inspector (26a4f0e4c56c586e542915b47c800e1c87a44fd8af3f08c92eb04107a2567ae4)
cutekitten-test@1.0.1 ships a preinstall lifecycle script (preinstall.js) that runs automatically on npm install. The script collects os.hostname() and os.userInfo().username and POSTs them as a formatted message to a hardcoded Discord webhook at canary.discord.com/api/webhooks/1566232728179843243/[...]. The destination is author-controlled and not configurable by the installer. The exfiltration fires on default install without any explicit user invocation, and the package provides no documented, caller-configurable alternative for the destination.
